chapter_summary: Proverbs 27 is a rich collection of wisdom on humility, friendship, diligence, and the brevity of human plans. It opens with a sharp warning against boasting about tomorrow, since no one controls what a day will bring. It moves through the wisdom of honest friendship — faithful wounds, timely counsel — contrasted with the danger of flattery and the foolishness of uncontrollable anger and envy. The chapter closes with an extended picture of agricultural stewardship: know the state of your flocks, care for what God has given you, and your household will have what it needs. Wealth and power do not last; faithful, diligent work does.
main_lesson: Do not boast about tomorrow. Be a faithful friend. Work hard and care well for what God has given you.

memory_verse.kjv: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
memory_verse.little_bible: Just as iron sharpens iron, a good friend makes you better.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 27 opens with one of Scripture's most honest reminders: you do not know what tomorrow holds (v. 1). This is not pessimism — it is wisdom. The humble person holds plans loosely, trusting God with what they cannot control. For your children, this is an early, vital lesson: boasting about the future is a form of pride because it assumes a control that belongs only to God.

The heart of the chapter is its teaching on friendship. Verses 5 and 6 distinguish between real love and false affection with startling clarity: an open rebuke is better than hidden love, and the wounds of a friend are faithful while an enemy's kisses are deceptive. Help your children understand that real friendship is not just comfort and agreement — it is honesty, even when honesty is uncomfortable. The friend who tells you when you are wrong is more valuable than the one who always tells you what you want to hear.

Verse 17 — iron sharpening iron — is perhaps the most memorable image of this chapter. True friendship is not passive. It is an active, sometimes uncomfortable, mutually improving relationship. Help your children pursue friendships that make them wiser, kinder, and more godly, not just friendships that are fun or easy.

The final section (vv. 23–27) shifts to the wisdom of faithful stewardship. Know what you have. Care for it well. Riches and crowns do not last, but the faithful diligence of daily work provides for those in your care. This is a picture of the responsible life — and a call to children to learn the dignity of caring well for whatever they have been entrusted with.
application_for_children: This week, be the kind of friend who tells the truth kindly. Look after what God has given you — your belongings, your responsibilities, your relationships. And do not boast about what you will do tomorrow; trust God with your plans.

verses.kjv: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
verses.little_bible: Do not brag about what you will do tomorrow. You do not know what tomorrow will bring. Only God knows.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not boast about tomorrow. Only God knows.
verses.meaning: Human beings are tempted to speak confidently about the future as if they control it, but the future belongs to God alone. Boasting about tomorrow is a subtle form of pride — an assumption of sovereignty that belongs only to God. James 4:13–14 echoes this truth directly. Wisdom holds plans with open hands.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You with tomorrow.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it unwise to brag about what you will do tomorrow?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to hold their plans loosely — making wise plans while trusting God with the outcome — without either passivity or presumptuous boasting?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something you planned to do. Say, 'I hope to do this if God wills it.' Practise holding plans with open hands.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child making grand plans with a speech bubble full of tomorrow's boasts, but a gentle divine hand holding a calendar only God can see, soft watercolour scene with wonder

verses.kjv: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
verses.little_bible: Let others praise you, not yourself. It is better when someone else says you did well. Do not praise yourself.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Let others praise you. Do not praise yourself.
verses.meaning: Self-praise is a form of pride and ultimately rings hollow. Genuine honour is conferred by others — it cannot be seized by the one who wants it. A person who praises themselves has no objective standing to do so; a stranger's praise, given freely, carries real weight. This is the wisdom of humility over self-promotion.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from praising myself too much.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it feel different when someone else praises you instead of yourself?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate genuine humility in our children — the ability to receive praise graciously and to let their work speak for itself rather than constantly promoting themselves?
verses.do_it_today: Today, instead of telling others something you did well, do good work quietly and let them notice on their own.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child working hard quietly while another child notices and points out the good work with admiration, warm and humble watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath is heavier than them both.
verses.little_bible: Stones are heavy. Sand is heavy too. But the anger of a foolish person is heavier than both. It is a terrible burden to bear.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A fool's anger is the heaviest burden of all.
verses.meaning: A fool's anger is not just unpleasant — it is oppressive and crushing to those around them. Unlike the manageable weight of stone or sand, the rage of a fool has no reason, no limit, and no relief. It is disproportionate and destructive. This is a warning against both being a fool in anger and being too close to one.
verses.prayer: God, help me control my anger wisely.
verses.discussion_question: How does a foolish person's anger feel to people around them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that uncontrolled anger is not just a personal failing but a burden imposed on those who have to live with it?
verses.do_it_today: When you feel angry today, stop before you act. Take a breath. Ask God to help you respond wisely, not foolishly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small child straining under the weight of a massive stone labelled 'a fool's anger', heavier than a huge pile of sand beside them, honest and vivid watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Wrath is cruel, and anger is outrageous; but who is able to stand before envy?
verses.little_bible: Anger is cruel and violent. But envy — wanting what others have — is even harder to stop. It destroys from the inside.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Envy is harder to stop than even fierce anger.
verses.meaning: Wrath and anger are visible and violent, but envy is a corrosive internal force that drives people to extremes that simple anger would not. Envy is behind many of the worst acts in human history — including the crucifixion of Jesus (Matthew 27:18). It is uniquely dangerous because it is hidden and relentless.
verses.prayer: God, free me from envy and jealousy.
verses.discussion_question: What makes envy different from and more dangerous than ordinary anger?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children recognise and root out envy early — noticing when wanting what others have is driving their feelings, and learning to bring that to God?
verses.do_it_today: Is there something someone else has that you are envying? Tell God about it honestly. Ask Him to help you be content.
verses.illustration_prompt: A dark shadowy figure of envy looming over two people arguing in anger, the envy figure larger and more menacing, honest watercolour scene with sombre tones

verses.kjv: Open rebuke is better than secret love.
verses.little_bible: It is better to tell someone clearly when they are wrong. Love that stays silent when it should speak is not truly helpful.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honest correction is better than silent love.
verses.meaning: A love that never corrects is not truly loving — it values the other person's comfort over their growth. Open rebuke, given in genuine love and concern, is a far greater gift than affection that stays silent when truth is needed. This is a challenge to the passive, conflict-avoiding version of love that refuses to speak hard truths.
verses.prayer: God, help me love others enough to speak truth.
verses.discussion_question: Is it always kind to say nothing when a friend is doing something wrong? Why not?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a family culture where honest, loving rebuke is welcomed as a gift — and where staying silent when truth is needed is understood as a failure of love?
verses.do_it_today: Is there someone you care about who needs a gentle, honest word? Pray about it. If God leads, speak kindly but clearly.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child gently but clearly telling a friend they have done wrong, the friend looking thoughtful rather than hurt, love and truth together, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.
verses.little_bible: A true friend's correction hurts a little, but it is faithful and good. An enemy may smile and flatter, but their kindness is a trick.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A friend's honest words are worth more than an enemy's flattery.
verses.meaning: The 'wounds of a friend' are the honest, corrective words that a true friend is willing to offer even when they cause pain. These wounds are faithful — they serve real love. By contrast, the enemy's kisses are deceptive — the outward warmth conceals destructive intent. Judas's kiss is the supreme example. Choose honest friends over flattering enemies.
verses.prayer: God, give me faithful friends who speak truth.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time a true friend said something hard but helpful to you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children distinguish between real friendship (which includes honesty) and false friendship (which only flatters and agrees)? What does true loyalty look like?
verses.do_it_today: Thank a friend who has ever told you the truth, even when it was hard to hear. Their honesty was a gift.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two children, one gently saying a hard truth with care, the other listening with trust — contrasted with a shadowy figure offering false smiles, warm and honest watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
verses.little_bible: A person who is already full does not want even sweet honey. But a person who is very hungry finds even bitter things taste good. Need changes everything.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: When you are hungry, even bitter food tastes good.
verses.meaning: This proverb observes a truth about human perception: our need shapes our experience. The full person can afford to be picky; the hungry person has no such luxury. Spiritually, this is a picture of why the self-sufficient refuse the Gospel while the desperate receive it gladly. Recognising our spiritual hunger is the beginning of wisdom.
verses.prayer: God, help me be hungry for Your Word.
verses.discussion_question: Why does food taste better when you are very hungry? What does that teach us?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children recognise spiritual hunger — a genuine need for God's Word and presence — rather than becoming spiritually 'full' and indifferent to what God offers?
verses.do_it_today: Before you read your Bible today, ask God to make you hungry to hear from Him. Come to it with need, not routine.
verses.illustration_prompt: A full child turning away from a honeycomb, contrasted with a hungry child eagerly eating even plain bread, both scenes honest and clear, gentle watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place.
verses.little_bible: A bird that leaves its nest is in danger. A person who wanders away from where they belong is also in danger.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Stay where you belong. Wandering brings danger.
verses.meaning: The bird's nest is its place of safety, purpose, and belonging. A bird without its nest is exposed and vulnerable. The proverb applies this to human rootlessness — whether geographic, relational, or spiritual. The person who wanders from their calling, their community, and their God is similarly exposed. Faithfulness to one's place is wisdom.
verses.prayer: God, help me stay rooted in You and my family.
verses.discussion_question: What dangers can come from wandering away from where you belong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a healthy sense of belonging and rootedness — in family, in church, in community — rather than the restless wandering that leaves people exposed?
verses.do_it_today: Are you drifting from something important — family, church, God's Word? Take one step back toward where you belong today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small bird flying away from its warm and safe nest into a cold open sky, looking lost and exposed, the nest glowing warmly in the background, tender watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel.
verses.little_bible: Sweet perfume makes the heart happy. In the same way, a friend who gives you kind and honest advice brings real joy to your heart.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A friend's wise advice refreshes like sweet perfume.
verses.meaning: The pleasure of good perfume or ointment is immediate and physical — it lifts the mood and brings delight. The proverb places heartfelt, wise counsel from a true friend in the same category of soul-refreshment. Good advice from someone who genuinely loves you is a sensory-level joy. This elevates the role of counsel and friendship to something beautiful and life-giving.
verses.prayer: God, give me friends who counsel me wisely.
verses.discussion_question: What makes advice from a true friend feel so good to receive?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create a family culture where counsel is welcomed and given — where asking for advice is seen as strength, and offering wise guidance is an act of love?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a trusted person for advice on something you are working through. Receive their counsel as a gift.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child receiving warm, kind advice from a trusted friend, both leaning in with care, the atmosphere fragrant and warm like perfume, glowing watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.
verses.little_bible: Do not abandon old and trusted friends. When trouble comes, a nearby friend may help you more than a far-away brother. Stay close to loyal people.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Keep old friends close. A near friend helps more than a far brother.
verses.meaning: This verse prizes longstanding, cultivated loyalty. Old friends — even friends of the previous generation — carry a depth of trust that cannot be replaced. In a crisis, proximity and faithful history matter more than family title without relationship. The neighbour who is present and proven is more valuable in the day of calamity than a brother who has never invested in the relationship.
verses.prayer: God, help me be faithful to my true friends.
verses.discussion_question: Why might a loyal nearby friend help you more in trouble than a distant relative?
verses.family_discussion: How do we invest in and cultivate deep, loyal friendships over years — not just for times of trouble, but as a reflection of God's faithful covenant love in human relationships?
verses.do_it_today: Reach out to a long-standing friend or family friend today. Invest in that relationship before you need it in a crisis.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child in distress being helped by a nearby faithful neighbour while a brother waves from far in the distance, the warmth and closeness of proven friendship glowing, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
verses.little_bible: My son, be wise. When you are wise, you make my heart glad. Your wisdom shows others that I have taught you well.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Be wise and make your parents glad.
verses.meaning: The father's joy in his child's wisdom is not purely personal — it has a public dimension. A wise child defends the parent's honour against those who might question their parenting or character. Every child's wisdom or foolishness reflects on those who raised them. This is a gentle motivation: your wise choices honour the people who love you and have invested in you.
verses.prayer: God, help me be wise and honour my parents.
verses.discussion_question: How does your wise behaviour honour and encourage the people who love and teach you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that their choices — for wisdom or foolishness — have an impact not just on themselves but on the family's name, reputation, and witness?
verses.do_it_today: Do one wise and kind thing today specifically because you want to honour and encourage your parents.
verses.illustration_prompt: A parent with a glowing, proud heart watching a child make a wise decision, the parent's face full of joy and honour, warm family watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself; but the simple pass on, and are punished.
verses.little_bible: A wise person sees danger coming and gets out of the way. A foolish person does not see it and keeps walking — and gets hurt.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people see danger and avoid it. Fools walk right into it.
verses.meaning: Wisdom includes foresight — the ability to see consequences and dangers before they arrive and to act accordingly. The prudent person does not wait for the disaster to hit before responding; they read the signs and prepare. The simple person has no such capacity — they walk forward blindly and suffer for it. This is a call to develop discernment, not just reaction.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom to see danger and choose right.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to foresee danger? How can wisdom help you avoid being hurt?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop foresight — the ability to think ahead about consequences, to see where a path is leading, and to make wise choices before a situation becomes a crisis?
verses.do_it_today: Think about a decision you are facing. What are the possible consequences? Ask God to help you see clearly before you decide.
verses.illustration_prompt: A wise child stepping aside as a danger passes, while another child walks straight into it without seeing it, the contrast clear and honest, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
verses.little_bible: If someone promises to pay a debt for a stranger or an untrustworthy person, be very careful. Make them give you something valuable as security.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Be careful about promises made for untrustworthy people.
verses.meaning: This proverb echoes Proverbs 20:16 — the financial wisdom of requiring collateral when someone has made a reckless guarantee for an unknown person. Co-signing for a stranger is imprudent; the person who does so has taken a serious risk. The text is a practical warning about financial entanglement with the untrustworthy. Wisdom in money matters is part of godly stewardship.
verses.memory_phrase: Be wise with promises and money.
verses.prayer: God, help me be wise and careful with every promise I make.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it risky to promise to pay someone else's debt when you do not know them well?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children wise stewardship in financial matters — including the danger of reckless guarantees, co-signing, and financial entanglement with untrustworthy people?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a parent about one wise money habit your family practises. Commit to learning and applying it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child handing over a garment as a pledge of security while making a careful agreement, the scene showing wisdom and caution in financial dealings, gentle watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
verses.little_bible: If you shout loud greetings at your friend very early in the morning, they will not think of it as kindness. Too much at the wrong time becomes annoying.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Loud blessings at the wrong time feel like a curse.
verses.meaning: Even a genuinely good thing — blessing a friend — becomes a nuisance when done with no regard for timing, context, or the other person's need. The excessive enthusiasm that wakes someone up with loud greetings is tone-deaf. Wisdom in relationships includes attentiveness to timing and proportion. Good intentions do not excuse poor judgment.
verses.prayer: God, help me be thoughtful about when and how I speak.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a kind thing that becomes annoying if done at the wrong time?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop social wisdom — the awareness that even good intentions can become burdensome if they ignore what others actually need in the moment?
verses.do_it_today: Before you say or do something for someone today, think about whether the timing and the way you do it will actually help them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child shouting cheerful greetings very loudly to a sleepy friend early in the morning, the friend looking annoyed despite the kind intent, warm but honest watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
verses.little_bible: A dripping roof on a rainy day never stops and drives you mad. A person who always wants to argue is just like that — exhausting and never-ending.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Constant arguing is like a dripping roof in rain.
verses.meaning: The image of a continuously dripping roof on a stormy day is one of relentless, inescapable irritation — you cannot stop it, you cannot ignore it, and there is no relief. Constant quarrelsomeness in a relationship has exactly this quality. It wears away peace, rest, and joy through sheer relentlessness. Contentious speech is destructive not by violence but by persistence.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose peace over arguing.
verses.discussion_question: How does someone who always argues affect the peace of a home or family?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate peace-seeking rather than quarrelsomeness in our family — understanding that constant contention is as destructive in its dripping way as any open conflict?
verses.do_it_today: Notice today how many times you are tempted to argue or start a dispute. Choose peace instead, even once.
verses.illustration_prompt: Water dripping relentlessly through a leaky roof into a bucket on a stormy day, a tired figure sitting beneath it looking worn out, honest and vivid watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, which bewrayeth itself.
verses.little_bible: Trying to stop a quarrelsome person is like trying to grab the wind. You cannot hold it. Their nature reveals itself no matter what.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: You cannot hide or stop a quarrelsome person.
verses.meaning: The contentious person described in verse 15 cannot be concealed or contained — like the wind, they cannot be grasped or suppressed; like strong perfume, they announce themselves no matter what. This is a realistic observation: certain deep patterns of character are self-revealing and cannot be hidden for long. It is also a warning about the limits of managing others' behaviour without heart change.
verses.prayer: God, change my heart so my character reflects You.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think a person's true character always comes out eventually?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that character — whether contentious or peaceable — cannot be hidden forever, and that the work of becoming good must happen from the inside out?
verses.do_it_today: Ask yourself: what does my character reveal when no one is watching? Ask God to shape you from the inside.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure trying to grasp and hold wind in their hands while perfume scent drifts through the air regardless — character revealing itself inevitably, thoughtful watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
verses.little_bible: Just as iron sharpens iron, a good friend helps make you better. True friends improve each other.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good friends make each other sharper and better.
verses.meaning: Two pieces of iron, when struck together, sharpen each other. This is the picture of real friendship: not merely pleasant companionship, but mutual sharpening — intellectual, moral, and spiritual. True friends challenge each other, provoke each other to growth, and make each other more capable. This is why the choice of friends is one of the most important decisions a person makes.
verses.prayer: God, give me friends who help me grow.
verses.discussion_question: How has a good friend ever helped you become better or wiser?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children intentionally choose friendships that sharpen them — friendships built on shared values, mutual honesty, and encouragement toward what is good?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one friend who makes you better. Tell them what you appreciate about them and how they have helped you grow.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two pieces of iron striking together sending bright sparks, then two friends laughing and growing wiser together, the image of mutual sharpening clear and warm, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
verses.little_bible: The person who tends a fig tree gets to eat its fruit. The person who faithfully serves their master will be honoured. Faithful work brings its reward.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Faithful service is always rewarded.
verses.meaning: The connection between diligent work and its reward is clear and reliable — as clear as the farmer who tends his fig tree receiving its fruit. The servant who faithfully serves will be honoured. This is not mere transactional thinking; it is the wisdom of covenant — faithfulness and its rewards are woven into the fabric of how God made the world.
verses.prayer: God, help me be faithful in every task I am given.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to faithfully care for something? What reward does it bring?
verses.family_discussion: How do we instil in our children the connection between faithful, diligent care and its fruits — and the patience required to wait for those fruits to appear?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one task or responsibility you have been given. Care for it faithfully today, even if no one is watching.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child carefully tending a fig tree over time and then joyfully eating its sweet fruit, faithfulness and reward shown in sequence, warm productive watercolour scene

verses.kjv: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
verses.little_bible: A face reflected in water shows you exactly what is there. People's hearts reflect each other too — what is in you, you often find in others.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: People's hearts reflect each other like water reflects faces.
verses.meaning: Water reflects accurately — it shows what is there. Similarly, human hearts have a remarkable ability to recognise themselves in others: we are drawn to those who share our nature, we recognise in others the depths (and the failings) that we know in ourselves. This is both a relational observation and a call to self-knowledge — understanding yourself helps you understand others.
verses.prayer: God, help me know my own heart and understand others.
verses.discussion_question: What do you think it means that people's hearts reflect each other?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate self-awareness in our children — the ability to understand their own heart well enough to have compassion for and insight into others?
verses.do_it_today: Look at yourself in a mirror. Then ask: what is truly in my heart today? Be honest with God about what you see.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child looking into still water and seeing their face reflected clearly, then looking at a friend and recognising something of themselves, thoughtful and beautiful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.
verses.little_bible: The grave is never full — it always takes more. In the same way, human eyes are never truly satisfied. Wanting more never ends.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Human eyes are never truly satisfied — they always want more.
verses.meaning: Sheol (the realm of the dead) and destruction are pictured as always hungry, always consuming, never satisfied. This is the picture of human craving and covetousness: the eyes are never satisfied. No amount of possession, achievement, or pleasure will fill the human soul's bottomless appetite. Only God can satisfy the deepest human longing — which is why covetousness and greed are ultimately spiritual problems.
verses.prayer: God, fill my heart. Help me stop wanting more and more.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think getting more and more things never makes people truly happy?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate contentment in our children — helping them recognise the insatiable nature of unchecked desire, and training them to find satisfaction in God rather than in more things?
verses.do_it_today: Look at what you already have today. Thank God for three specific things. Practise being satisfied.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child's eyes always looking toward the next thing, more and more objects piling up but never filling the space, the emptiness behind the wanting clear, honest watercolour scene

verses.kjv: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.
verses.little_bible: Fire tests silver and gold and shows what they truly are. Praise tests a person and shows their true character. How you handle praise reveals who you are.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Praise tests a person's true character.
verses.meaning: The refining pot reveals the quality of the metal — impurities become visible under heat. Praise performs the same function in human character: it reveals whether a person is genuinely humble, self-controlled, and mature, or whether they are vain, proud, and unstable. How someone handles being praised is a reliable test of their character.
verses.prayer: God, help me stay humble when people praise me.
verses.discussion_question: How can the way a person responds to praise reveal what they are truly like inside?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children receive praise well — neither dismissing it falsely nor being puffed up by it — as an expression of genuine, tested humility?
verses.do_it_today: The next time someone praises you today, practise saying 'thank you' simply — neither deflecting nor boasting. Just receive it with humble gratitude.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crucible of fire testing silver and revealing its purity, beside a child receiving praise and staying calm and humble, the parallel clear and warm, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, yet will not his foolishness depart from him.
verses.little_bible: Even if you ground a foolish person like grain in a mortar, their foolishness would not leave them. Foolishness goes very deep into a person's heart.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Deep foolishness does not go away easily.
verses.meaning: This is one of the bluntest proverbs in the book: some people's foolishness is so deeply entrenched that no external force — not pressure, punishment, or suffering — will remove it. The only change that removes deep foolishness is a changed heart, which only God can give. This is a warning about the limits of correction without repentance and transformation.
verses.memory_phrase: Only God can change a fool's heart.
verses.prayer: God, change my heart so foolishness does not rule me.
verses.discussion_question: Why can foolishness be so hard to change? What does only God have the power to do?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that lasting change from foolishness to wisdom is a work of God's grace — and that this is why we pray for hearts to be changed, not just behaviour to be corrected?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God to change something foolish in your own heart today. Be honest with Him about it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A mortar and pestle grinding grain, but a shadow of foolishness remaining even after the grinding, the stubbornness of deep foolishness shown honestly, sober watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.
verses.little_bible: Be diligent. Know the state of what is in your care. Look carefully after the things and people God has given you to tend.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Know what God has given you to care for. Look after it well.
verses.meaning: This is a call to active, attentive stewardship. The farmer must know his flock — not just in a general way, but intimately, specifically, with ongoing attention. Neglect is the enemy of good stewardship. The principle extends beyond livestock to every area of responsibility: family, work, finances, gifts, relationships. What God has entrusted to us requires our sustained, knowledgeable attention.
verses.memory_phrase: Know and care for what is yours.
verses.prayer: God, help me care well for what You have given me.
verses.discussion_question: What things or people has God given you to care for and look after well?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children the habit of attentive, diligent stewardship — knowing the state of what they are responsible for and caring for it faithfully rather than neglecting it?
verses.do_it_today: Look around at what you are responsible for — belongings, relationships, tasks. Notice one thing that needs more care. Give it that care today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A shepherd carefully counting and checking each sheep in the flock at sunset, attentive and diligent, the flock safe and well-tended, warm pastoral watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For riches are not for ever: and doth the crown endure to every generation?
verses.little_bible: Riches do not last for ever. Even crowns and kingdoms do not last from one generation to the next. Only faithful work and God's blessing endure.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Riches and crowns do not last for ever.
verses.meaning: This is a sober and realistic assessment: wealth is not permanent, and political power does not automatically transfer to the next generation. This is the justification for verse 23 — because material wealth is uncertain, the diligent cultivation of productive resources (flocks, skills, relationships) is wiser than depending on stored-up riches. The call is to build what endures, not what fades.
verses.memory_phrase: Riches do not last for ever.
verses.prayer: God, help me build what truly lasts in Your kingdom.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we not put all our trust in money or power? What lasts longer?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children hold material wealth lightly — understanding its impermanence — while investing in what genuinely endures: character, faithfulness, and God's kingdom?
verses.do_it_today: Think of something you have trusted in that could disappear. Now think of one thing that will last for ever. Which one are you building?
verses.illustration_prompt: A crown and a pile of gold slowly fading and crumbling, while a diligent worker tending a field and family stands firm and bright, honest contrast in watercolour

verses.kjv: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
verses.little_bible: The hay appears and the new grass grows. Herbs from the hills are gathered in their season. God provides what is needed at the right time.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God provides grass, herbs, and hay in their season.
verses.meaning: This verse is part of the agricultural sequence (vv. 25–27) that shows the faithful rhythm of God's provision in creation. Hay, grass, and mountain herbs all appear in their proper season — a picture of God's reliable, cyclical provision. The wise steward works within this rhythm, trusting that faithful diligence will be met by God's faithful provision.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for providing for us in every season.
verses.discussion_question: How does the way God makes grass and plants grow teach us to trust Him?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see the rhythms of creation — seasons, growth, harvest — as expressions of God's ongoing faithful provision, and to trust Him through every cycle of life?
verses.do_it_today: Go outside and notice something growing. Thank God for providing through creation. Trust Him with your own needs.
verses.illustration_prompt: Fresh green grass appearing after the dry season, mountain herbs gathered by a diligent farmer, new growth and provision in a hopeful pastoral watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The lambs are for thy clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
verses.little_bible: The lambs give you wool for clothing. The goats can be sold to buy more land. Faithful care of what you have provides what you need.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Caring for your flocks provides clothing and resources.
verses.meaning: This continues the agricultural portrait: every part of what the diligent person tends has purpose and value. Lambs provide wool; goats provide income and the means to acquire more land. The principle is that faithful stewardship of present resources becomes the basis for future provision and expansion. Nothing is wasted when it is wisely cared for.
verses.memory_phrase: Care well and you will have enough.
verses.prayer: God, help me care well for what You have given me.
verses.discussion_question: How does caring for what you have now help provide what you need later?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children that faithful stewardship of present resources — time, gifts, relationships, finances — is the path to future provision and flourishing?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one resource you have — time, a skill, a possession. How can you steward it better today to produce good results later?
verses.illustration_prompt: Lambs with soft wool ready for shearing, goats healthy and strong at the edge of a green field, faithful provision from careful tending, warm pastoral watercolour scene

verses.kjv: And thou shalt have goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and for the maintenance for thy maidens.
verses.little_bible: Faithful care of your goats will give you enough milk. There will be enough for you, your family, and all who depend on you. Diligence feeds your whole household.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Faithful diligence provides enough for your whole family.
verses.meaning: The closing verse of the chapter is a promise of sufficiency — not excess, but enough. The diligent person who tends their flock faithfully will have food for themselves, their family, and their servants. This is the vision of faithful stewardship: God's blessing on diligent, attentive work provides for all who depend on you. Enough, given faithfully, is God's good design.
verses.prayer: God, bless my diligent work to care for those around me.
verses.discussion_question: What does it look like when someone works faithfully and provides enough for their whole family?
verses.family_discussion: How do we close the loop with our children between the diligence they practise now and the future provision for others that their faithfulness will enable? How does faithful work become an act of love for family and community?
verses.do_it_today: Work hard at one task today with your family or household in mind. Offer your effort to God as a way of caring for the people around you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A family gathered around a table with goats' milk and simple food in abundance, the faithful farmer and their household provided for, warmth and contentment in a joyful watercolour scene
